name: Rice-paper cheese bourekas (בורקס דפי אורז וגבינות)

source.author: Hebrew recipe (pasted)
source.notes: No-dough 'bourekas': each one is a single rice-paper sheet dipped in an egg-honey-water wash (for crunch), filled with a cottage/Bulgarian/cheese-mix + egg filling, folded envelope-style, egg-washed and sesame+nigella topped, baked 220°C ~25 min. No frying. Analyzed per boureka; batch assumed to make ~8 (filling ~260 g, ~1 tbsp each). Bulgarian + cheese mix taken at standard (not light) fat. Estimate — 'play with the cheeses' means macros vary. Optimization in suggested_mods / chat.

ingredients.note: dipped, not soaked — a few seconds only
very salty — go easy on added salt; verify pasteurized
the fat/sodium lever — 'play with what's in the fridge'
helps browning/crisp; a little added sugar

steps: Mix all the filling ingredients (cottage, Bulgarian, cheese mix, egg, s&p) to a uniform mix.
In a shallow plate mix the dip: egg, honey and a little water.
Dip one rice paper in the dip a few seconds until slightly softened (not too much).
Lay it on the counter, put a spoon of filling in the center and fold into a rectangle (envelope).
Place on greased parchment, folds facing UP (keeps it crisp).
Brush each boureka with beaten egg, sprinkle sesame + nigella.
Bake 220 °C ~25 min until deep golden and very crispy.

batch_totals.note: ~8 bourekas. The Bulgarian + cheese mix drive the fat, saturated fat and sodium; the rice paper is a light wrapper (no dough). Baked, not fried. 'Play with the cheeses' changes these a lot — leaner cheeses drop fat/sodium sharply.

him.verdict: A clever no-dough, baked (not fried) cheese pastry — the rice-paper wrapper keeps the carbs light and there's no fried oil, which is the good part. But the filling is cheese-heavy: the Bulgarian + yellow/mozzarella mix make it fat- and sodium-forward, so per boureka it's ~6.4 g protein for ~127 kcal (~5 g protein per 100 kcal) with ~6 g fat and little fiber. Fine as a tasty snack / light bite, not a protein anchor. Very easy to lean out — shift the cheese ratio toward cottage + light cheeses (see mods) and it climbs to ~8.
flags: ~6.4 g protein / 127 kcal (~5 g protein per 100 kcal)
baked, not fried — no added frying oil (good)
cheese-heavy: ~6 g fat/boureka (~3.5 g saturated), Bulgarian + yellow mix
low fiber — refined rice-paper wrapper; honey adds a little sugar
suggested_mods: Shift the cheese ratio: more cottage, use LIGHT Bulgarian 5% + part-skim mozzarella, less full-fat yellow — more protein, far less fat/sodium
Skip the added salt entirely (Bulgarian covers it); the honey in the dip can be halved
Fold chopped spinach / parsley + za'atar into the filling — adds folate + fiber the pastry lacks
These are great for portion control — log by the piece; 2–3 is a reasonable snack

her_preconception.verdict: A calcium- and protein-contributing cheese pastry, fully baked (egg filling + wash cooked through), so broadly fine. The one flag is the Bulgarian cheese — a brined soft cheese: it's baked through here (cooked = considered safe) and most Israeli Bulgarit is pasteurized, but verify it. Not a big prenatal-nutrient source on its own; folding in spinach would turn it into a real folate contributor.
prenatal_highlights: calcium + protein from the cheeses + egg
fully baked; some choline from the eggs

safety_advisories.note: Bulgarian cheese is a brined soft cheese — Listeria risk unless pasteurized. It's baked through here (considered safe cooked); verify pasteurized.
safety_advisories.swap: verify pasteurized / keep baked through, or shift to more cottage + mozzarella

suggested_mods: Fold spinach into the filling for folate + iron
Verify the Bulgarian is pasteurized; serve with tomato/pepper for vitamin C

cooking_guide: Mix the filling (cottage, crumbled Bulgarian, cheese mix, 1 egg, pepper) to a uniform mix. Go easy on salt — the Bulgarian is already very salty; taste before adding any.
Make the dip in a shallow plate: 1 egg + 1 tbsp honey + a little water, whisked. The egg-honey wash is the crunch secret and it helps the bourekas brown.
Dip ONE rice paper in the wash for just a few seconds — until slightly pliable, not fully soft. Over-dipping makes it tear and go gummy.
Lay it flat, put ~1 tbsp filling in the center (don't overfill or it bursts) and fold into a rectangle like an envelope.
Place on greased parchment with the FOLDS FACING UP — this keeps the base flat and the whole thing crisp.
Brush each with beaten egg and sprinkle sesame + nigella.
Bake at 220 °C (or Ninja Grill on Bake) ~25 min until deep golden and very crispy. Rice paper crisps fast at the end, so watch the last few minutes.
Tips: shift the cheese toward cottage + light cheeses for a leaner version; fold in chopped spinach or parsley + za'atar for flavor, folate and a bit of fiber.
